targetChunk: have + just + past participle (news just now)
clozeTemplate: ___ ___ ___ the report to Deniz.
situationTr: [Ayşe'ye Teams mesajı] Raporu Deniz'e az önce gönderdin ve haber veriyorsun: "Raporu Deniz'e daha yeni gönderdim."
acceptedAnswers: I've just sent the report to Deniz.
I've just sent Deniz the report.
I just sent the report to Deniz.
I just sent Deniz the report.
modelSentences: I've just sent the report to Deniz.
I've just updated the ticket with the new logs.
We've just finished the regression run.
commonMistake: I have just send the report to Deniz.
checklistTr: Doğru yapıyı seçtin mi? (have + V3: sent, send değil)
Yardımcı fiil doğru mu? (I've / I have)
just, have'den sonra ve V3'ten önce mi?
noteTr: Türkçe 'gönderdim' hem 'sent' hem 'have sent' karşılığıdır; haberi şimdiye bağlayan just ile have + V3 kullanılır. Bağlama göre AmE'de just / already / yet ile yalın geçmiş (I just sent) de yaygındır.
verifiedNote: verifier 2026-10-23: Cambridge Grammar present perfect simple: recent past events 'often use words like just or recently'. Oxford yet, usage note already/just/yet: in North American English also used with the simple past (rule 6b, so 'I just sent' is accepted). SkELL 'I've just sent' = 8 natural lines. Mistake (have + base form) is a common learner error, never correct. Fix: noteTr ellipsis removed and the too-absolute 'no other freedom' claim dropped.

targetChunk: past simple with ago (finished time)
clozeTemplate: I ___ this phone two weeks ago.
situationTr: [Arkadaşına] Telefonunu iki hafta önce aldığını söylüyorsun: "Bu telefonu iki hafta önce aldım."
acceptedAnswers: I bought this phone two weeks ago.
I bought this phone 2 weeks ago.
I got this phone two weeks ago.
I got this phone 2 weeks ago.
modelSentences: I bought this phone two weeks ago.
We moved to the new office three days ago.
Mert called me ten minutes ago.
commonMistake: I have bought this phone two weeks ago.
checklistTr: ago ile yalın geçmiş zaman kullandın mı? (bought, have bought değil)
Fiilin düzensiz geçmiş biçimini yazdın mı? (buy -> bought)
ago, süreden sonra mı? (two weeks ago)
noteTr: Türkçe '-dim' hem yalın geçmişi hem present perfect'i karşılar; ama 'iki hafta önce' gibi bitmiş bir zamanla yalnız past simple kullanılır. Bağlama göre bought yerine got da denir.
verifiedNote: verifier 2026-10-23: Cambridge Grammar ago: 'We normally use ago with the past simple. We don't use it with the present perfect.' Longman ago GRAMMAR: present perfect with ago is a Don't-say form, so the mistake is genuine. Fix: added 'got ... 2 weeks ago' to match the existing digit variant.

targetChunk: There haven't been + noun + so far
clozeTemplate: There ___ ___ any failures so far.
situationTr: [Stand-up] Şu ana kadar hiç test hatası çıkmadığını söylüyorsun: "Şimdiye kadar hiç hata olmadı."
acceptedAnswers: There haven't been any failures so far.
There haven't been any test failures so far.
There haven't been any errors so far.
There have been no failures so far.
There have been no test failures so far.
So far there haven't been any failures.
modelSentences: There haven't been any failures so far.
We haven't had any complaints so far.
There haven't been any delays so far.
checklistTr: so far ile present perfect kullandın mı? (have been, were değil)
there + have mi? (çoğul isim -> There have/haven't been)
Olumsuzda any (haven't ... any) ya da no (have been no) seçtin mi?
noteTr: Türkçe 'olmadı' geçmiş kipiyle söylenir; 'şimdiye kadar' süreci bugüne bağladığı için İngilizcede present perfect kullanılır. Bağlama göre failures yerine errors da olur; AmE konuşmada yalın geçmiş de duyulur ama burada kabul edilmez (kural 6b).
verifiedNote: verifier 2026-10-23: Cambridge Grammar present perfect simple lists 'so far' with this use. Ngram (en-2019, 2010-19): 'were no problems so far' = 36% of 'been no problems so far', 'so far there were' = 51% of 'so far there have been', so the past simple with so far is too frequent in print to be shown as a clear error: commonMistake removed (rule 6b still keeps it out of the accepted list). Fixes: 'problems' variant replaced (its wording matched a book exercise line) by errors / test failures variants, word-order variant added, noteTr says AmE past simple is heard.

targetChunk: have + past participle + since + point in time
clozeTemplate: ___ ___ on this project since March.
situationTr: [Yeni birine] Bu projede Mart'tan beri çalıştığını söylüyorsun: "Mart'tan beri bu proje üzerinde çalışıyorum."
acceptedAnswers: I've worked on this project since March.
I've been working on this project since March.
I've been on this project since March.
modelSentences: I've worked on this project since March.
Deniz has been on leave since Monday.
We've used Jira since the start of the year.
commonMistake: I am working on this project since March.
checklistTr: since ile present perfect kullandın mı? (have worked / have been working, am working değil)
have / has doğru mu? (I've, he has)
since sonrasında başlangıç noktası mı? (March; süre için for)
noteTr: Türkçe 'Mart'tan beri çalışıyorum' şimdiki zamanla söylenir; İngilizcede since ile present perfect gerekir. Bağlama göre worked ve been working ikisi de olur.
verifiedNote: verifier 2026-10-23: Cambridge Grammar present perfect typical errors: 'They've known each other since January. Not: They know / They're knowing each other since January' (same error as the mistake). Longman since GRAMMAR: since + point in time. Ngram 'am working here since' = 0 vs 'have been working here since'. No change.

targetChunk: have + past participle + for + duration
clozeTemplate: ___ ___ in this flat for two years.
situationTr: [Komşuna] Bu dairede iki yıldır oturduğunuzu söylüyorsun: "Bu dairede iki yıldır oturuyoruz."
acceptedAnswers: We've lived in this flat for two years.
We've been living in this flat for two years.
We've lived in this apartment for two years.
We've been living in this apartment for two years.
modelSentences: We've lived in this flat for two years.
Mert has worked in QA for five years.
We've waited for the approval for two days.
commonMistake: We live in this flat for two years.
checklistTr: for ile present perfect kullandın mı? (have lived, live değil)
have / has doğru mu? (We have)
for süreden önce mi? (for two years; since değil)
noteTr: Türkçe 'iki yıldır oturuyoruz' şimdiki zamanla söylenir; İngilizcede süre için for ile present perfect gerekir. Bağlama göre flat BrE, apartment AmE'dir.
verifiedNote: verifier 2026-10-23: Cambridge Grammar present perfect typical errors: present simple/continuous are not used for time up to now; Cambridge past simple page: present perfect + for + period ('has been empty for three years'). Fixes: situationTr 'oturduğunu' -> 'oturduğunuzu' (we), added 'been living in this apartment'.

targetChunk: It's + time + since + past simple
clozeTemplate: ___ ___ ___ since we last updated the test data.
situationTr: [Ayşe'ye] Test verisini en son üç hafta önce güncellediğinizi söylüyorsun: "Test verisini en son güncelleyeli üç hafta oldu."
acceptedAnswers: It's three weeks since we last updated the test data.
It's been three weeks since we last updated the test data.
It has been three weeks since we last updated the test data.
It's been three weeks since we updated the test data.
It's three weeks since we updated the test data.
modelSentences: It's three weeks since we last updated the test data.
It's two days since the build last passed.
It's been a month since we released the hotfix.
commonMistake: We haven't updated the test data since three weeks.
checklistTr: Kalıp It's / It's been + süre + since mi? (since three weeks değil)
since'ten sonra yalın geçmiş kullandın mı? (we last updated)
Süre çoğul mu? (three weeks)
noteTr: Türkçe '-eli üç hafta oldu' kalıbı İngilizcede It's / It's been + süre + since + yalın geçmiş olur; since'ten sonra süre (three weeks) gelmez. Bağlama göre It's ve It's been ikisi de olur, last da atlanabilir.
verifiedNote: verifier 2026-10-23: Cambridge Grammar since: 'It's been years since I rode a bike (it's = it has)' and 'It's years since I rode a bike (it's = it is)'. Old mistake 'Three weeks passed since...' replaced: Ngram 'three years passed since' = 3.7% of 'three years have passed since' and it can be read as narrative past. New mistake uses since + period, which Cambridge marks wrong ('Not: ... since three years') and Longman since GRAMMAR says not to use. Fixes: added two variants without 'last', checklist reordered so the main clause (critical point, blanked in the cloze) is first, modelBlanks now blank It's / It's been.

targetChunk: present continuous for fixed arrangements (future)
clozeTemplate: ___ ___ the fix to staging tomorrow morning.
situationTr: [Ayşe'ye] Takvimde yazılı kesin plan: yarın sabah düzeltmeyi staging'e alıyorsunuz. "Yarın sabah düzeltmeyi staging'e alıyoruz."
acceptedAnswers: We're deploying the fix to staging tomorrow morning.
Tomorrow morning we're deploying the fix to staging.
We're deploying the fix to the staging environment tomorrow morning.
We're pushing the fix to staging tomorrow morning.
modelSentences: We're deploying the fix to staging tomorrow morning.
I'm meeting the product owner at four.
Deniz is taking the afternoon off on Friday.
checklistTr: Ayarlanmış plan için be + -ing kullandın mı? (We're deploying)
be doğru mu? (We're / We are; Deniz is)
Gelecek zaman belirteci var mı? (tomorrow morning)
noteTr: Türkçede ayarlanmış plan '-iyoruz' ya da '-eceğiz' ile söylenebilir; İngilizcede önceden ayarlanmış plan için en doğal biçim present continuous'tır (We're deploying). Bağlama göre will ya da going to da yanlış değildir ama bu kalıbı sınamaz.
verifiedNote: verifier 2026-10-23: Cambridge Grammar future: present continuous 'shows that we have already decided something and usually that we have already made a plan or arrangements'. Old commonMistake 'We will deploy the fix...' is correct English (the old noteTr itself said will is heard), so it was removed. Fixes: added 'pushing' variant (staging'e almak has no fixed verb), noteTr rewritten ('aynı ekle' was wrong: -iyoruz and -eceğiz are two suffixes).

targetChunk: be going to + base verb (decision already made)
clozeTemplate: ___ ___ ___ ask Ayşe to review the PR this afternoon.
situationTr: [Mert'e] Dün karar vermiştin: bu öğleden sonra Ayşe'den PR'ı incelemesini isteyeceksin. "Bu öğleden sonra Ayşe'den PR'ı incelemesini isteyeceğim."
acceptedAnswers: I'm going to ask Ayşe to review the PR this afternoon.
I'm going to ask Ayşe to review my PR this afternoon.
I'm going to ask Ayşe to look at the PR this afternoon.
I'm going to ask Ayşe to review the pull request this afternoon.
modelSentences: I'm going to ask Ayşe to review the PR this afternoon.
We're going to rerun the suite after lunch.
Deniz is going to write the test plan.
commonMistake: I going to ask Ayşe to review the PR this afternoon.
checklistTr: Önceden verilmiş karar için be going to kullandın mı? (will değil)
be unutulmadı mı? (I'm going to)
going to'dan sonra yalın fiil mi? (ask)
noteTr: Türkçe '-eceğim' hem anlık hem önceden verilmiş kararı karşılar; önceden verilmiş karar için İngilizcede be going to kullanılır. Bağlama göre konuşmada I'm gonna duyulur, ama yazıda going to yazılır.
verifiedNote: verifier 2026-10-23: Cambridge Grammar be going to: 'Usually the decision about the future plans has already been made'; will is used for decisions at the moment of speaking. Missing 'be' (I going to) is a common learner error, never correct. Fix: noteTr wording ('yazıda to' -> 'yazıda going to').

targetChunk: present simple for timetables (future)
clozeTemplate: The last train ___ at eleven tonight.
situationTr: [Arkadaşına] Tarifeye göre son tren bu gece saat on birde kalkıyor: "Son tren bu gece on birde kalkıyor."
acceptedAnswers: The last train leaves at eleven tonight.
The last train leaves at 11 tonight.
The last train departs at eleven tonight.
The last train leaves tonight at eleven.
The last train is at eleven tonight.
The last train goes at eleven tonight.
modelSentences: The last train leaves at eleven tonight.
The sprint review starts at ten tomorrow.
The demo ends at four on Friday.
checklistTr: Tarifedeki olay için yalın şimdiki zaman kullandın mı? (leaves)
Üçüncü tekil -s var mı? (the train leaves)
Saat edatı at doğru mu?
noteTr: Türkçede tarifeye bağlı gelecek olay '-ıyor' ya da '-ecek' ile söylenir; İngilizcede tarife ve programdaki olaylar için yalın şimdiki zaman (leaves) kullanılır. Bağlama göre departs daha resmîdir; will leave yanlış değildir ama bu kalıbı sınamaz.
verifiedNote: verifier 2026-10-23: Cambridge Grammar future present simple: used for 'a clear or fixed schedule or timetable: The train arrives at 20.12'. SkELL 'the last train leaves' has natural lines. Fixes: commonMistake null removed (the schema rejects null; no mistake is right because will leave is correct), added BrE 'goes', noteTr rewritten, dailyContext changed from a habitual sentence (opens on Saturdays) to a future timetable sentence.

targetChunk: as soon as + present simple, will + base verb
patternSlots: As soon as the build ___, I'll ...
clozeTemplate: As soon as the build ___, I'll send you the link.
situationTr: [Mert'e] Build bitince linki göndereceksin: "Build biter bitmez sana linki göndereceğim."
acceptedAnswers: As soon as the build finishes, I'll send you the link.
I'll send you the link as soon as the build finishes.
As soon as the build is done, I'll send you the link.
I'll send you the link as soon as the build is done.
As soon as the build is finished, I'll send you the link.
I'll send you the link as soon as the build is finished.
As soon as the build has finished, I'll send you the link.
I'll send you the link as soon as the build has finished.
modelSentences: As soon as the build finishes, I'll send you the link.
As soon as I get the logs, I'll look at them.
I'll ping you as soon as Deniz replies.
commonMistake: As soon as the build will finish, I'll send you the link.
checklistTr: as soon as'tan sonra yalın şimdiki zaman kullandın mı? (finishes, will finish değil)
Ana cümlede will / 'll var mı? (I'll send)
Üçüncü tekil -es doğru mu? (the build finishes)
noteTr: Türkçe 'biter bitmez' gelecekteki bir olayı anlatsa da İngilizcede as soon as / when / if'ten sonra gelecek için will kullanılmaz; yalın şimdiki zaman gelir. Bağlama göre finishes yerine is done, is finished ya da has finished de olur.
verifiedNote: verifier 2026-10-23: Cambridge Grammar Conjunctions: time: 'We don't use will after conjunctions referring to future time ... Not: ... as soon as I will get to the office'; Cambridge when: present simple or present perfect in the time clause. Ngram 'as soon as it will' = 0.51% of 'as soon as it is'. Fixes: added is finished / has finished variants (correct, were marked wrong); model 3 reworded because it matched a book exercise frame.

targetChunk: if + present simple, will + base verb
clozeTemplate: If the test ___ again, I'll open a bug.
situationTr: [Ayşe'ye] Test tekrar kalırsa bug açacaksın: "Test yine kalırsa bir bug açacağım."
acceptedAnswers: If the test fails again, I'll open a bug.
If the test fails again, I'll log a bug.
I'll open a bug if the test fails again.
I'll log a bug if the test fails again.
If the test fails again, I'll raise a bug.
I'll raise a bug if the test fails again.
If the test fails again, I'll file a bug.
I'll file a bug if the test fails again.
modelSentences: If the test fails again, I'll open a bug.
If you need the logs, I'll send them over.
If the deploy breaks anything, we'll roll back.
commonMistake: If the test will fail again, I'll open a bug.
checklistTr: if'ten sonra yalın şimdiki zaman kullandın mı? (fails, will fail değil)
Sonuç cümlesinde will / 'll var mı? (I'll open)
Üçüncü tekil -s var mı? (the test fails)
noteTr: Türkçe '-ırsa / -erse' ekinden sonra gelecek anlamı olsa da İngilizcede if cümlesinde will kullanılmaz, yalın şimdiki zaman gelir. Bağlama göre open a bug yerine log, raise ya da file a bug da denir.
verifiedNote: verifier 2026-10-23: Cambridge Grammar Conditionals: if: 'Not: If a lawyer will read the document'. Ngram 'if it will rain' = 4.3% of 'if it rains' (includes correct indirect questions like 'I wonder if it will rain'), so the dictionary rule is the main evidence. Fixes: added raise / file a bug (established bug collocations used in earlier batches), noteTr wording.

targetChunk: when + present simple, will + base verb
clozeTemplate: When Ayşe ___, we'll start dinner.
situationTr: [Arkadaşına] Ayşe gelince akşam yemeğine başlayacaksınız: "Ayşe gelince yemeğe başlarız."
acceptedAnswers: When Ayşe arrives, we'll start dinner.
When Ayşe gets here, we'll start dinner.
When Ayşe comes, we'll start dinner.
We'll start dinner when Ayşe arrives.
We'll start dinner when Ayşe gets here.
We'll start dinner when Ayşe comes.
When Ayşe arrives, we'll start eating.
We'll start eating when Ayşe arrives.
modelSentences: When Ayşe arrives, we'll start dinner.
When the release is ready, I'll tell the team.
When Deniz joins the call, we'll begin.
commonMistake: When Ayşe will arrive, we'll start dinner.
checklistTr: when'den sonra yalın şimdiki zaman kullandın mı? (arrives, will arrive değil)
Ana cümlede will / 'll var mı? (we'll start)
Üçüncü tekil -s var mı? (Ayşe arrives / gets)
noteTr: Türkçe 'gelince' gelecekteki olayı anlatır, ama İngilizcede when'den sonra will gelmez; yalın şimdiki zaman kullanılır. Bağlama göre arrives yerine gets here ya da comes, start dinner yerine start eating da olur.
verifiedNote: verifier 2026-10-23: Cambridge Grammar when: 'we use the present simple or the present perfect in the when-clause ... Not: When the new park will open, I'll go there every day'. Ngram 'start dinner when' / 'start eating when' both attested. Fixes: added comes and start eating variants (direct translations of gelince / yemeğe başlamak).

targetChunk: Do you know where + subject + verb (indirect question)
clozeTemplate: Do you know where ___ ___ ___ ___ saved?
situationTr: [Deniz'e Teams'te] Test raporunun nereye kaydedildiğini soruyorsun: "Test raporunun nereye kaydedildiğini biliyor musun?"
acceptedAnswers: Do you know where the test report is saved?
Do you know where the test report is stored?
Do you know where the test report is kept?
Do you know where the test report was saved?
Could you tell me where the test report is saved?
Can you tell me where the test report is saved?
modelSentences: Do you know where the test report is saved?
Do you know when the stand-up ends?
Could you tell me which environment Deniz is using?
commonMistake: Do you know where is the test report saved?
checklistTr: where'den sonra düz cümle sırası kullandın mı? (the test report is, is the test report değil)
İç soruda do/does/is öne alınmadı, değil mi?
Giriş kalıbı doğru mu? (Do you know / Could you tell me)
noteTr: Türkçe 'nereye kaydedildiğini biliyor musun' kalıbında soru sırası yoktur; İngilizcede dolaylı soruda özne fiilden önce gelir (where the report is). Bağlama göre saved yerine stored / kept, Do you know yerine daha kibar Could you tell me da olur.
verifiedNote: verifier 2026-10-23: Cambridge Grammar reported speech (indirect speech): the reported question is in statement form (subject + verb), with Not: examples for inverted order. Longman tell: 'Can you tell us where the nearest garage is?'. Ngram 'know where is the' = 0.23% of 'know where the'. Fixes: added 'was saved' (kaydedildiğini), noteTr names the order.

targetChunk: Could you tell me how + subject + verb (polite indirect question)
patternSlots: Could you tell me how I ___ ...?
clozeTemplate: Could you tell me how ___ ___ get access to the staging environment?
situationTr: [Ayşe'ye Teams'te] Staging ortamına nasıl erişim alabileceğini kibarca soruyorsun: "Staging ortamına nasıl erişim alabileceğimi söyleyebilir misin?"
acceptedAnswers: Could you tell me how I can get access to the staging environment?
Can you tell me how I can get access to the staging environment?
Could you tell me how I could get access to the staging environment?
Could you tell me how I can access the staging environment?
Could you let me know how I can get access to the staging environment?
Can you let me know how I can get access to the staging environment?
Would you tell me how I can get access to the staging environment?
modelSentences: Could you tell me how I can get access to the staging environment?
Could you tell me when the release is planned?
Can you tell me why the build failed?
commonMistake: Could you tell me how can I get access to the staging environment?
checklistTr: how'dan sonra özne + yardımcı fiil sırası mı? (how I can, how can I değil)
Kibar giriş kalıbı doğru mu? (Could you tell me)
get access to: to unutulmadı mı?
noteTr: İngilizcede Could you tell me ile başlayan soruda içteki soru düz cümle sırasına döner (how I can, how can I değil). Bağlama göre Could you let me know da kullanılır; how to get access da doğrudur ama bu kalıbı sınamaz.
verifiedNote: verifier 2026-10-23: Cambridge Grammar reported speech: statement word order with when, where, why and how, Not: inverted. Ngram 'tell me how can I' = 4.3% of 'tell me how I can' (part is direct speech after a comma). Fixes: added 'how I could get access' and 'how I can access'; noteTr explains that 'how to get access' is correct but skips the target (rule 2.2/2).

targetChunk: What happened + to (question without did)
clozeTemplate: What ___ to your laptop?
situationTr: [Ayşe'ye] Ayşe'nin laptopu bozuk görünüyor; ne olduğunu soruyorsun: "Laptopuna ne oldu?"
acceptedAnswers: What happened to your laptop?
What's happened to your laptop?
What has happened to your laptop?
What happened with your laptop?
modelSentences: What happened to your laptop?
What changed in the last release?
Who approved the change?
commonMistake: What did happen to your laptop?
checklistTr: Özne sorusunda did kullanmadın mı? (What happened, What did happen değil)
Fiil geçmiş biçimde mi? (happened)
Edat to doğru mu? (happened to)
noteTr: Türkçe 'ne oldu' tek fiille sorulur; İngilizcede sorulan şey özneyse did eklenmez (What happened?). Bağlama göre happened to ile happened with ikisi de duyulur.
verifiedNote: verifier 2026-10-23: Cambridge Grammar wh-questions: 'When what, who, which or whose is the subject ... we do not use the auxiliary'. Cambridge happen: happen + to + object ('What's happened to your jacket?'). Ngram 'what did happen to' = 0.23% of 'what happened to' (rest is contrastive emphasis, not a neutral question). No change.

targetChunk: a for first mention, the for second mention
clozeTemplate: I opened ___ ticket yesterday. ___ ticket is still unassigned.
situationTr: [Mert'e] Dün bir ticket açtın ve onun hâlâ kimseye atanmadığını söylüyorsun: "Dün bir ticket açtım. Ticket hâlâ kimseye atanmadı."
acceptedAnswers: I opened a ticket yesterday. The ticket is still unassigned.
Yesterday I opened a ticket. The ticket is still unassigned.
I opened a ticket yesterday. The ticket still isn't assigned.
I opened a ticket yesterday. The ticket still hasn't been assigned.
I opened a ticket yesterday. The ticket isn't assigned yet.
I opened a ticket yesterday. The ticket hasn't been assigned yet.
Yesterday I opened a ticket. The ticket still hasn't been assigned.
modelSentences: I opened a ticket yesterday. The ticket is still unassigned.
I saw a bug on the login page. The bug only happens in Chrome.
Mert wrote a script. The script restarts the server.
commonMistake: I opened ticket yesterday. Ticket is still unassigned.
checklistTr: İlk sözde a, ikinci sözde the kullandın mı?
Tekil sayılabilir isimden önce tanımlık var mı? (a ticket, ticket değil)
İkinci cümlede fiil uyumu doğru mu? (the ticket is)
noteTr: Türkçede a / the karşılığı yoktur, 'bir' de çoğu zaman düşer; İngilizcede tekil sayılabilir isim ilk geçişte a, aynı şeye ikinci kez değinirken the alır. Bağlama göre ikinci cümle isn't assigned yet ya da hasn't been assigned ile de kurulur.
verifiedNote: verifier 2026-10-23: Cambridge Grammar A/an and the: a/an when the thing is 'not already known', the when it is 'already known' to the listener. Fixes: noteTr had 3 sentences and said Turkish 'bir' is only for emphasis (wrong); one-sentence 'and/but the ticket' variants (unnatural repeat of the noun) replaced by the natural ways to say atanmadı (isn't assigned yet / hasn't been assigned); model 2 'in the login page' -> 'on the login page' (Ngram on = 2.8x in).

targetChunk: a / an before a job title
clozeTemplate: Deniz is ___ test engineer in our team.
situationTr: [Yeni gelen birine] Deniz'in ekibinizde test mühendisi olduğunu söylüyorsun: "Deniz ekibimizde bir test mühendisi."
acceptedAnswers: Deniz is a test engineer in our team.
Deniz is a test engineer on our team.
Deniz is a QA engineer in our team.
Deniz is a QA engineer on our team.
Deniz's a test engineer in our team.
modelSentences: Deniz is a test engineer in our team.
Mert is a developer on the payments team.
Ayşe is an automation engineer.
commonMistake: Deniz is test engineer in our team.
checklistTr: Meslekten önce a / an kullandın mı? (a test engineer)
a / an seçimi sesli harfe göre mi? (a test, an engineer)
Edat doğru mu? (in / on our team)
noteTr: Türkçede 'mühendis' önünde tanımlık gerekmez; İngilizcede meslek tekil sayılabilir isimdir ve a / an alır. Bağlama göre QA engineer de denir; in our team daha çok BrE, on our team AmE'dir.
verifiedNote: verifier 2026-10-23: Cambridge Grammar A/an and the: 'When we talk about a person's job, we use a: She's a gardener'. Ngram 'on our team' = 3.3x 'in our team'; SkELL 'on our team' 259 lines, both accepted. Article omission before a job is a common learner error. Fix: noteTr names the in/on team BrE/AmE difference.

targetChunk: Most + plural noun (no the)
clozeTemplate: ___ users don't read the release notes.
situationTr: [Ayşe'ye] Kullanıcıların çoğunun sürüm notlarını okumadığını söylüyorsun: "Kullanıcıların çoğu sürüm notlarını okumuyor."
acceptedAnswers: Most users don't read the release notes.
Most users don't read release notes.
Most users don't bother to read the release notes.
Most users don't bother reading the release notes.
Most of our users don't read the release notes.
Most of the users don't read the release notes.
modelSentences: Most users don't read the release notes.
Most bugs appear after a deployment.
Most teams use Jira for planning.
commonMistake: The most users don't read the release notes.
checklistTr: Genel anlamda most'tan önce the kullanmadın mı? (Most users, The most users değil)
most + çoğul isim ve çoğul fiil mi? (users don't)
Olumsuz yapı doğru mu? (don't + yalın fiil)
noteTr: The most en üstünlük bildirir (the most important); 'çoğu' anlamında genel konuşurken most + çoğul isim kullanılır ve the gelmez. Bağlama göre most of our / most of the users da doğrudur.
verifiedNote: verifier 2026-10-23: Cambridge Grammar Most, the most, mostly: most + noun for the majority in general, 'Not: ... on the most days'; Oxford most: 'Most of the people I had invited turned up'. SkELL 'most users don't' = 11 natural lines; Ngram 'the most people' = 0.78% of 'most people'. Fixes: 'Kullanıcıların çoğu' directly elicits most of the / most of our users, which are correct, so both added; noteTr rewritten (old reason 'Türkçe çoğu has no article' did not explain the error).

targetChunk: There was / were + noun (existence)
clozeTemplate: ___ ___ a delay on the metro this morning.
situationTr: [Geç kalınca arkadaşına] Bu sabah metroda gecikme olduğunu söylüyorsun: "Bu sabah metroda bir gecikme vardı."
acceptedAnswers: There was a delay on the metro this morning.
There was a delay on the subway this morning.
There was a delay on the underground this morning.
There were delays on the metro this morning.
There were delays on the subway this morning.
There were delays on the underground this morning.
modelSentences: There was a delay on the metro this morning.
There was a problem with the login page.
There were three failures in the last run.
commonMistake: It was a delay on the metro this morning.
checklistTr: 'Vardı' için There was / were kullandın mı? (It was değil)
there'den sonra tekil / çoğul uyumu doğru mu? (a delay -> was; delays -> were)
Edat doğru mu? (on the metro)
noteTr: Türkçe 'vardı' tek sözcüktür ve özne gerektirmez; İngilizcede varlık için there özne olarak yazılır (It was değil). Bağlama göre metro, subway ve underground bölgeye göre değişir.
verifiedNote: verifier 2026-10-23: Cambridge Grammar There is, there's and there are: 'There's a letter on your desk ... Not: It's a letter on your desk'. Ngram 'it was a delay' = 2% of 'there was a delay' (other meanings). Fixes: added 'delays on the underground'; dailyContext replaced twice (the draft line and a first replacement were both close to book example lines).

targetChunk: There's no / There isn't any + noun (absence)
clozeTemplate: ___ no response from the API.
situationTr: [Deniz'e Teams'te] API'den hiç yanıt gelmediğini söylüyorsun: "API'den hiç yanıt yok."
acceptedAnswers: There's no response from the API.
There isn't any response from the API.
There's no reply from the API.
There isn't any reply from the API.
modelSentences: There's no response from the API.
There's no data for that date.
There isn't any documentation for this endpoint.
commonMistake: It's no response from the API.
checklistTr: 'Yok' için There is no / isn't any kullandın mı? (It's no değil)
no + isim ya da isn't any + isim; ikisini karıştırmadın mı?
from the API: edat from doğru mu?
noteTr: Türkçe 'yok' tek sözcüktür; İngilizcede yokluk there is no + isim ile söylenir, it ile söylenmez. Bağlama göre There's no ve There isn't any aynı anlamdadır.
verifiedNote: verifier 2026-10-23: Cambridge Grammar There is, there's: 'Not: It's a letter on your desk'; Cambridge No more: 'There's no more cake (or There isn't any more cake)' shows no = not any. SkELL 'there is no response from' = 12 lines. Fixes: targetChunk named the canonical form, added 'isn't any reply', noteTr ellipsis removed.

targetChunk: There will be + noun (future existence)
clozeTemplate: ___ ___ ___ time for questions at the end of the demo.
situationTr: [Katılımcılara] Demonun sonunda soru için zaman ayrılacağını söylüyorsun: "Demonun sonunda soru sormak için zaman olacak."
acceptedAnswers: There will be time for questions at the end of the demo.
There'll be time for questions at the end of the demo.
There will be time for questions after the demo.
There'll be time for questions after the demo.
There will be some time for questions at the end of the demo.
modelSentences: There will be time for questions at the end of the demo.
There will be a short break after the first session.
There'll be an update on Friday.
commonMistake: Will be time for questions at the end of the demo.
checklistTr: 'Olacak' için There will be kullandın mı? (will be tek başına değil)
there özne olarak yazıldı mı? (There will be ... / There'll be ...)
time sayılamaz mı? (time for questions; a time değil)
noteTr: Türkçede özne düşer ('zaman olacak'); İngilizcede varlık cümlesinde there özne olarak yazılır. Bağlama göre There will be ve There'll be aynıdır, kısaltma daha konuşma tarzıdır.
verifiedNote: verifier 2026-10-23: SkELL 'There will be time for questions' = 5 natural lines; Cambridge There is, there's and there are: there as subject for existence. Dropping the dummy subject is a typical error of pro-drop L1 learners (Turkish). Normaliser does not expand there'll, so both forms stay listed. Fix: added 'some time' variant.

targetChunk: has / have been + past participle (passive, current result)
clozeTemplate: The deployment ___ ___ postponed until Monday.
situationTr: [Ekip kanalında] Deploy'un Pazartesi'ye ertelendiğini duyuruyorsun: "Deploy Pazartesi gününe ertelendi."
acceptedAnswers: The deployment has been postponed until Monday.
The deployment's been postponed until Monday.
The deployment has been postponed to Monday.
The deployment has been moved to Monday.
The deployment has been put off until Monday.
The deployment has been delayed until Monday.
The deploy has been postponed until Monday.
modelSentences: The deployment has been postponed until Monday.
The bug has been fixed in the latest build.
The tests have been rescheduled for tomorrow.
commonMistake: The deployment has postponed until Monday.
checklistTr: Edilgen has / have been + V3 kullandın mı? (has been postponed)
has / have özneyle uyuşuyor mu? (deployment tekil -> has; tests çoğul -> have)
Fiil üçüncü biçimde mi? (postponed)
noteTr: Türkçe '-ildi' edilgeni İngilizcede be + V3 ile kurulur; bugüne etkisi süren bu duyuruda has been + V3 doğaldır (has postponed değil). Bağlama göre postponed yerine put off, delayed ya da moved da kullanılır.
verifiedNote: verifier 2026-10-23: Longman postpone: transitive, 'The match had to be postponed until next week'; Cambridge Passive: forms lists present perfect has/have been. Ngram 'has postponed until' = 2.4% of 'has been postponed until'; 'been moved to Monday' = 83% and 'been postponed to Monday' = 17% of 'until Monday', so both added; 'deploy' as a noun added (situationTr says Deploy). noteTr 'gerekir' softened. 'was postponed' left out per rule 6b.

targetChunk: was / wasn't + past participle (passive, no agent)
clozeTemplate: ___ ___ told about the schedule change.
situationTr: [Ekip kanalında] Takvim değişikliğinden sana haber verilmediğini söylüyorsun: "Takvim değişikliğinden bana haber verilmedi."
acceptedAnswers: I wasn't told about the schedule change.
I wasn't informed about the schedule change.
I wasn't informed of the schedule change.
I wasn't told about the change to the schedule.
I wasn't told about the change in the schedule.
modelSentences: I wasn't told about the schedule change.
We weren't given enough time to test it.
The team wasn't asked about the new process.
commonMistake: I didn't told about the schedule change.
checklistTr: Edilgen was / wasn't + V3 kullandın mı? (I wasn't told)
Olumsuzda didn't yerine wasn't mi? (didn't told değil)
Edat doğru mu? (told about)
noteTr: Türkçe 'bana haber verilmedi' cümlesinde özne yoktur; İngilizcede kişi özne olur ve was not + V3 kullanılır (I wasn't told). Bağlama göre told yerine informed (about / of) daha resmîdir.
verifiedNote: verifier 2026-10-23: Cambridge Grammar Passive: forms (past simple was/were + -ed form). SkELL 'wasn't told about' = 9 lines; 'didn't told' appears only in 3 non-native web lines, so the mistake is a real learner form. Ngram 'not informed of the' = 1.9x 'not informed about the'. Fixes: added 'informed of' and 'change in the schedule'; noteTr quoted 'söylenmedi' but the situationTr says 'haber verilmedi'.

targetChunk: not ... anything (no double negative)
clozeTemplate: I ___ buy ___ at the market.
situationTr: [Arkadaşına] Pazardan hiçbir şey almadığını söylüyorsun: "Pazardan hiçbir şey almadım."
acceptedAnswers: I didn't buy anything at the market.
I didn't buy anything from the market.
I bought nothing at the market.
I didn't buy a thing at the market.
modelSentences: I didn't buy anything at the market.
I haven't changed anything in the config.
We didn't find anything unusual in the logs.
commonMistake: I didn't buy nothing at the market.
checklistTr: Olumsuz cümlede anything kullandın mı? (didn't ... anything; nothing ile çift olumsuz yapma)
Olumsuz yardımcı doğru mu? (didn't + yalın fiil: buy)
Ya da olumlu fiil + nothing kullandın mı? (I bought nothing)
noteTr: Türkçede 'hiçbir şey almadım' çift olumsuzdur; İngilizcede bir cümlede tek olumsuzluk olur: didn't + anything ya da bought + nothing. Bağlama göre ikisi de doğrudur, didn't buy anything daha yaygındır.
verifiedNote: verifier 2026-10-23: Cambridge Grammar Double negatives and usage: in standard English a negative word is not used with a negative verb ('Not: He hadn't nothing ...'). Ngram 'did not buy nothing' = 1.25% of 'did not buy anything'. Fixes: added 'from the market' (Pazardan), model 3 'Let me know if you need anything' replaced (not a negative sentence and it matched a book line), noteTr ellipses removed.

targetChunk: probably + won't (adverb position)
clozeTemplate: We ___ ___ go to the cinema tonight.
situationTr: [Arkadaşına] Bu akşam sinemaya büyük ihtimalle gitmeyeceksiniz: "Bu akşam büyük ihtimalle sinemaya gitmeyeceğiz."
acceptedAnswers: We probably won't go to the cinema tonight.
We probably won't go to the movies tonight.
We probably won't go to the cinema this evening.
We probably won't go to the movies this evening.
We'll probably not go to the cinema tonight.
We'll probably not go to the movies tonight.
modelSentences: We probably won't go to the cinema tonight.
I probably won't finish the review today.
Deniz will probably join the call late.
commonMistake: We won't probably go to the cinema tonight.
checklistTr: probably, won't'tan önce mi? (probably won't; won't probably değil)
Olumsuz kısaltma doğru mu? (won't = will not)
won't'tan sonra yalın fiil mi? (go)
noteTr: Türkçede sözcük sırası serbesttir ('gitmeyeceğiz büyük ihtimalle'); İngilizcede probably olumlu will'den sonra, olumsuzda won't'tan önce (ya da will probably not) gelir. Bağlama göre cinema BrE, movies AmE'dir.
verifiedNote: verifier 2026-10-23: Cambridge Grammar Adverbs: position: probably goes in mid position ('It'll probably rain'). SkELL 'probably won't' = 2070 lines vs 'won't probably' = 8; Ngram 'will not probably' = 0.64% of 'probably will not', but 'will probably not' = 26%, so it is correct and was added. Fix: noteTr mentions will probably not.

targetChunk: no longer / not ... any more
clozeTemplate: Ayşe ___ ___ works on this project.
situationTr: [Yeni gelen birine] Ayşe'nin artık bu projede çalışmadığını söylüyorsun: "Ayşe artık bu projede çalışmıyor."
acceptedAnswers: Ayşe no longer works on this project.
Ayşe doesn't work on this project any more.
Ayşe doesn't work on this project anymore.
Ayşe doesn't work on this project any longer.
Ayşe isn't working on this project any more.
Ayşe isn't working on this project anymore.
Ayşe is no longer working on this project.
modelSentences: Ayşe no longer works on this project.
The old test environment no longer exists.
We don't use that script any more.
commonMistake: Ayşe no more works on this project.
checklistTr: no longer ya da not ... any more kullandın mı? (no more değil)
no longer ana fiilden önce mi? (no longer works); any more sonda mı?
Üçüncü tekil doğru mu? (works / doesn't work)
noteTr: Türkçe 'artık çalışmıyor' tek yapıdır; İngilizcede no longer ana fiilden önce, not + any more ise cümle sonunda gelir. Bağlama göre any more (BrE) ve anymore (AmE) ikisi de yazılır.
verifiedNote: verifier 2026-10-23: Cambridge Grammar No longer, not any longer: no longer in mid position; Cambridge Any more or anymore: adverb any more in end position, anymore especially AmE. Old mistake 'works no more' replaced: Oxford more marks 'no more (= no longer)' as formal and Ngram 'she lives no more' exists, so it can be correct. 'he no more works' = 0 in Ngram vs 'he no longer works', so the mid-position form is a clear error. Fixes: added any longer and present continuous variants, noteTr ellipsis removed.

targetChunk: hasn't + past participle + yet / still hasn't
clozeTemplate: Mert ___ replied to my message ___.
situationTr: [Ayşe'ye Teams'te] Mert'in mesajına henüz yanıt vermediğini söylüyorsun: "Mert mesajıma henüz yanıt vermedi."
acceptedAnswers: Mert hasn't replied to my message yet.
Mert still hasn't replied to my message.
Mert hasn't answered my message yet.
Mert hasn't responded to my message yet.
Mert didn't reply to my message yet.
modelSentences: Mert hasn't replied to my message yet.
The build hasn't finished yet.
I haven't received the approval yet.
commonMistake: Mert has not reply to my message yet.
checklistTr: hasn't + V3 kullandın mı? (hasn't replied, hasn't reply değil)
yet olumsuz cümlenin sonunda mı? (still ise hasn't'ten önce)
has / have özneyle uyuşuyor mu? (Mert -> has; I -> have)
noteTr: Türkçe 'henüz yanıt vermedi' geçmiş kipiyle söylenir; İngilizcede yet ile present perfect kullanılır. Bağlama göre replied yerine answered da olur; AmE'de didn't reply yet de duyulur, ama yazıda hasn't replied daha güvenlidir.
verifiedNote: verifier 2026-10-23: Oxford yet: '(British English) I haven't received a letter from him yet. (North American English) I didn't receive a letter from him yet'; Oxford usage note: some Americans do not accept the simple past here, which supports the noteTr advice. AmE form accepted per rule 6b. Have + base form is a common learner error. Fixes: added answered / responded variants.
